questions.q: Statements: All roses are flowers. No flowers are plants. Conclusions: I. All roses are plants. II. No roses are plants.
questions.why: Checked against every possible diagram of the statements: I need not be true, II must be true. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: What comes next in the series? 4, 6, 10, 18, 34, …
questions.why: Each term is ×2 − 2. Next: 66. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Sunil walks 9 m West, then turns left and walks 4 m, then turns right and walks 4 m. Which direction is Sunil facing now?
questions.why: Follow each turn from the first direction: the last leg is towards the West. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Find the wrong number in the series: 45, 52, 61, 66, 73, 80, 87
questions.why: In the correct series each term adds 7, so 61 should be 59. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Peter and Beckon walk in the same direction. Peter's speed is 5 km/h and Beckon's 6 km/h. If Peter starts 3 km behind Beckon, after how many hours will they be 17 km apart?
questions.why: The gap grows by 1 km/h, from 3 to 17: 14 hours. GPSC JSO pre-screening, Jun 2026.

questions.q: What is the angle between the hands of a clock at 7:45?
If 15 July 2020 was a Wednesday, what day of the week was 22 September 2020?
questions.why: 69 days later; 69 mod 7 = 6, so count 6 days on from Wednesday. GPSC-style practice item.

questions.q: Should trade unions be banned completely? I. Yes, workers can concentrate on production. II. No, it is the only way employees can put demands to management. III. Yes, unions get illegal demands met. IV. No, advanced countries don't ban them.
opts: Only I and II are strong
Only I, II and III are strong
questions.why: II gives a real, important reason. I and III are weak generalisations; IV just copies others. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2024.
